author: NBCPhiladelphia
title: Japan rice crisis shows signs of easing as prices stabilize and stocks return to shelves
text:
Rice prices in Japan have started to ease, falling below Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s target of below 4,000 yen for a five-kilogram bag.
Prices of a five-kg bag of rice in supermarkets have dipped below 4,000 yen, the lowest in about two months.However, rice prices in Japan still remained elevated, with a Tokyo resident saying rice prices had increased sharply.Data from Japan's agriculture ministry
He recounted that a five-kilo bag of ice cost about 1,800 yen to 2,000 yen two years ago, but prices have more than doubled to between 4,500 and 5,000 yen. But supply recovery has been uneven, with rice shortage persisting in some places. Roy Larke, professor of Japan business at Tokyo-based intelligence firm JapanConsulting.com, told CNBC that some supermarkets around Tokyo still have empty rice displays, but these are small stores.
